text: I've been trying to get better about regularly going to a salon for a hair cut. For years I just went to Great Clips once a year. My stylist recommended that I start using a hair diffuser whenever I dry my hair because I have naturally curly hair. I don't use heat on my hair often but when I do, I've been attaching this to my hair dryer. I have the Infiniti Pro by Conair 1875 Watt Full Size Salon Performance AC Motor Styler/Hair Dryer (that I also bought from Amazon) and this fits on it perfectly. I read reviews that sometimes this hair diffuser doesn't work on all hair dryers because the diameter is smaller or larger than what this is compatible. But I measured the diameter of my hair dryer so I knew it would work. And I love how my hair reacts to being diffused. My curls just look marvelous. To attach, I ended up putting the diffuser on the floor, pressing the barrel of my blowdryer into the attachment tube, and sort of peeling the attachment onto the dryer. My fingers got pinched and scraped in the process, and I pretty much had to put my full bodyweight into it. If my partner had been home, I would have asked him to do it since he used to throw people for fun (cheerleader) and would have had the required strength in one arm. Even so, it took me a solid 5 minutes of bodyweight and a few minutes of Googling to figure out if maybe the diffuser just wouldn't work with my dryer, or if I was doing it wrong. I haven't used the diffuser yet. It just got here 10 minutes ago. I'll update when I've used it a few times. **EDIT** I've now used this diffuser twice. It stays on well enough while I'm using it, but as someone else mentioned: collapsible means holding the diffuser the whole time anyway, because it keeps collapsing during use. Also, be prepared to go through the painful process of reattaching it EVERY time you want to use it. When I lay my dryer down when I'm done, at least 1/3 of the edge of the diffuser slips off the barrel every time. And although I no longer need to use my bodyweight and I've tried other ways of attaching the diffuser, the only one that works is getting my fingers in the silicone attachment ring of the diffuser and stretching it over my dryer. Doesn't sound like a big deal, but this material doesn't stretch well-- as a result, my index fingers and thumbs are visibly scraped, and one index nail got smashed between diffuser and dryer hard enough that one side of the nail is detached and bleeding. A+ job making this "universal" diffuser attachable by the women it's meant for, dev team!

It does collapse on you a bit while drying but the ability to store it easily made it worth it to me. I’ve probably used it about 50 times. Today, I smelled a burning smell and looked down and the whole base had ripped. I’m pretty disappointed because this curly girl had to leave the house with a wet head and I’m just not sure if I should get another one…

title: Best Product Purchase Since Going Natural!
text: Love love love! I have an expensive Hot Tools blow dryer that came with a diffuser attachment that I absolutely loved. However, I bought The Curly Co diffuser because I was going on a trip to Europe and didn't want to lug my blow dryer and huge attachment around. This diffuser blew my mind! I've been using it ever since! The flat surface really lets my curls sit naturally to dry them without disturbing the pattern. The way that it collapses to get different angles makes diffusing super easy and nowhere near as akward as my old attatchment. This is seriously THE BEST hair purchase I have made since going natural a year ago. Simply the best!
